title: Broadway's big movie musical keeps breaking records. Is it worth $179 a ticket? Find out:Roma Review
transcript: Hit or miss before you go. Roma's Reviews - now you know! When I stepped out into the bright sunlight from the darkness of the movie house, I had only two things on my mind. Paul Newman and a ride home. Two years into its Broadway run, The Outsiders is overcoming and beating the odds. The 2024 Tony Award winner for best musical has not only recouped its investment, but it's broken the Bernard B. Jacobs Theatre's house record 10 times, becoming the first production in the theater's history to gross more than $2 million in a single week. And the tour is giving public school kids a chance to see it for free! S.E. Hinton's novel read by school kids nationwide also inspired the 1983 cult film directed by Francis Ford Coppola. As musical adaptations go, The Outsiders jumps to the head of the class. Everything about this production feels original and dynamic. Directed by Danya Taymor, it's a terrific collaboration highlighting all of the novel's virtues while side-stepping most of the clunkier aspects. Key to the success of the production is the excellent score composed by Jamestown Revival; Jonathan Clay and Zach Chance, along with Justin Levine, who's got a huge hand in the show. Each song is woven seamlessly into the narrative. The staging is another huge plus. Director Taymor keeps the action moving with flare and gritty authenticity. Add to all of this thrilling fight choreography under the direction of Rick and Jeff Kuperman. With muscular athleticism, their dance movements are powerful and evocative. The climactic rumble in the rain between the waring gangs is an extended ballet that's as fittingly violent as it is graceful. No worries about testosterone levels with this company. The Outsiders is an emotionally and viscerally satisfying work. You can see it on Broadway at least until the end of next January 2027. And as the national tour travels through the country, it is giving back to its communities through the Stay Gold Project. Educators in select tour cities can apply for free student tickets. Just visit your local theater or log on to outsidersusical.com/state-gold for details.
reasoning: Roma praises nearly every element — score, staging, direction, fight choreography — and calls it 'emotionally and viscerally satisfying.' Clear strong recommendation with no significant caveats.
